title: These Symptoms Send Japanese People to the Doctor
paragraphs: When people feel sick, they have to decide whether to see a doctor or to take medicine from a drugstore. A new survey shows which symptoms make people in Japan go to the doctor.

The survey was done by Intage Healthcare, a market research company in Tokyo. In April and May, it asked people aged 16 to 79 in the Tokyo and Osaka areas about 32 different health problems. A total of 2,523 people answered.

The number one reason to see a doctor was a high fever. About 84% of people said they would go to a doctor for this. For most people, a temperature of 38 degrees Celsius or higher was the point at which they decided to see a doctor. When their temperature was 37 point something, only about 20% thought about getting medical help.
Chronic headaches were the second most common reason to see a doctor. Rashes and other skin problems were third.
People had two main reasons for going to a doctor. They wanted a doctor to tell them what was wrong, and they wanted to get a prescription.

For other problems, many people used medicine from a drugstore. For example, 62.5% of people used this kind of medicine for headaches that they only had sometimes. Many people also used it for colds, sore throats and low fevers.
However, more than 30% of people did not take any medicine for occasional headaches or low fevers. They just rested until they felt better.
